question: The mirror formula is 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. If u = -20 cm and v = 20 cm, find f:
explanation: 1/f = 1/20 + 1/(-20) = 0 — wait, recalculate: 1/f = 1/20 - 1/20 = 0 is wrong. Correct: 1/f = -1/20 + 1/20 = 0? Check: for u=-20, v=20: 1/f = 1/20 + 1/(-20) = 0. Actually if f = -10: 1/(-10) = -0.1, but 1/20 - 1/20 = 0. Let me reconsider: if virtual image v=+20 (upright) and object u=-20 (real), then mirror is concave (converging). 1/f = 1/20 + 1/(-20) means... no. Convention: u is -ve for real object. 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = 1/20 + 1/(-20) = 0? That can't be right. Let me check again. Actually, for a concave mirror with u=-20 (real), if v=+20 (virtual upright image), then 1/f = 1/(+20) + 1/(-20) = 1/20 - 1/20 = 0 is nonsensical. Re-examine: maybe v should be negative for real inverted image. If v=-20 (real, inverted): 1/f = 1/(-20) + 1/(-20) = -2/20 = -1/10, so f = -10 cm (concave). This makes sense.
subject: Science
